1. INTRODUCTION
Biological laboratories generate valuable measurements for predicting molecular interactions, pro-
tein responses and cellular perturbations. Privacy and data-sharing constraints often require these
measurements to remain at their original institutions (Sheller et al., 2020; Bakhtiari et al., 2025).
How can laboratories use their collective experimental evidence to improve a predictor while retain-
ing their own data? Beyond fitting shared parameters, we aim to automate a second part of model
development: choosing and revising prediction components and training configurations using feed-
back from participating laboratories. This calls for a collaborative research process in which local
evidence informs both model training and the next design experiment.
